The **1990s** (often referred to as and shortened to "**the '90s**" or "**the Nineties**") was a [decade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decade "Decade") that began on 1 January 1990, and ended on 31 December 1999. Known as the "[post-Cold War decade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post%E2%80%93Cold_War_era "Post–Cold War era")", the 1990s were culturally imagined as the period from the [Revolutions of 1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutions_of_1989 "Revolutions of 1989") until the [September 11 attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks "September 11 attacks") in 2001.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s#cite_note-1) The [dissolution of the Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Soviet_Union "Dissolution of the Soviet Union") marked the end of Russia's status as a [superpower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superpower "Superpower"), the end of a [multipolar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polarity_(international_relations) "Polarity (international relations)") world, and the rise of [anti-Western sentiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Western_sentiment "Anti-Western sentiment"). China was still recovering from a politically and economically turbulent period, allowing the US to [emerge as the world's sole superpower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superpower#Post-Cold_War_era "Superpower"), creating relative [peace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace "Peace") and [prosperity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s_economic_boom "1990s economic boom") for many western countries.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s#cite_note-2) During this decade, the [world population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_population "World population") grew from 5.3 to 6.1 billion.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s#cite_note-3)

The decade saw greater attention to [multiculturalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiculturalism "Multiculturalism") and advance of [alternative media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_media "Alternative media"). Public education about [safe sex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safe_sex "Safe sex") curbed [HIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV "HIV") in developed countries. [Generation X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generation_X "Generation X") bonded over musical tastes. Humor in television and film was marked by ironic [self-references](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-reference "Self-reference") mixed with [popular culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_culture "Popular culture") references. Alternative music movements like [grunge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grunge "Grunge"), [reggaeton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggaeton "Reggaeton"), [Eurodance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurodance "Eurodance"), [K-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-pop "K-pop"), and [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop"), became popular, aided by the rise in [satellite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satellite_television "Satellite television") and [cable television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cable_television "Cable television"), and the [internet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet "Internet"). New music genres such as [drum and bass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_and_bass "Drum and bass"), [post-rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-rock "Post-rock"), [happy hardcore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happy_hardcore "Happy hardcore"), _[denpa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denpa\_song "Denpa song")_, and [trance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trance_music "Trance music") emerged. Video game popularity exploded due to the development of [CD-ROM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CD-ROM "CD-ROM") supported [3D computer graphics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3D_computer_graphics "3D computer graphics") on platforms such as [Sony PlayStation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_(console) "PlayStation (console)"), [Nintendo 64](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_64 "Nintendo 64"), and [PCs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_computer "Personal computer").

The 1990s saw [advances in technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s_in_technology "1990s in technology"), with the [World Wide Web](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Wide_Web "World Wide Web"), evolution of the [Pentium microprocessor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentium_(original) "Pentium (original)"), rechargeable [lithium-ion batteries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithium-ion_battery "Lithium-ion battery"), the first [gene therapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_therapy "Gene therapy") trial, and [cloning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloning "Cloning"). The [Human Genome Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Genome_Project "Human Genome Project") was launched in 1990, by the [National Institutes of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Institutes_of_Health "National Institutes of Health") (NIH) with the goal to sequence the entire human genome.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s#cite_note-4) Building the [Large Hadron Collider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_Hadron_Collider "Large Hadron Collider"), the world's largest and highest-energy [particle accelerator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_accelerator "Particle accelerator"), commenced in 1998, and [Nasdaq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasdaq "Nasdaq") became the first US stock market to trade online.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s#cite_note-7)Environmentalism is divided between left-wing [green politics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_politics "Green politics"), [primary industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_industry "Primary industry")-sponsored environmentalist [front organizations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Front_organization "Front organization"), and a more business-oriented approach to the regulation of [carbon footprint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_footprint "Carbon footprint") of businesses. More businesses started using [information technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_technology "Information technology").

There was a realignment and consolidation of economic and political power, such as the continued mass-mobilization of [capital markets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_market "Capital market") through [neoliberalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoliberalism "Neoliberalism"), [globalization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Globalization "Globalization"), and end of the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War"). Network cultures were enhanced by the proliferation of new media such as the internet, and a new ability to self-publish web pages and make connections on professional, political and hobby topics. The [digital divide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_divide "Digital divide") was immediate, with access limited to those who could afford it and knew how to operate a computer. The internet provided anonymity for individuals skeptical of the government. Traditional mass media continued to perform strongly. However, mainstream internet users were optimistic about its benefits, particularly the future of [e-commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-commerce "E-commerce"). [Web portals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_portal "Web portal"), a curated bookmark homepage, were as popular as searching via [web crawlers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_crawler "Web crawler"). The [dot-com bubble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dot-com_bubble "Dot-com bubble") of 1997–2000 brought wealth to some [entrepreneurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entrepreneur "Entrepreneur") before its [crash of the early-2000s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock_market_downturn_of_2002 "Stock market downturn of 2002").

Many countries were economically prosperous and spreading [globalization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Globalization "Globalization"). [High-income countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank_high-income_economy "World Bank high-income economy") experienced steady growth during the [Great Moderation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Moderation "Great Moderation") (1980s—2000s). Using a [mobile phone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_phone "Mobile phone") in a public place was typical [conspicuous consumption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conspicuous_consumption "Conspicuous consumption"). In contrast, the [GDP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GDP "GDP") of [former Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-Soviet_states "Post-Soviet states") states declined as a result of neoliberal restructuring. [International trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_trade "International trade") increased with the establishment of the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union") (EU) in 1993, [North American Free Trade Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_Free_Trade_Agreement "North American Free Trade Agreement") (NAFTA) in 1994, and [World Trade Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Organization "World Trade Organization") (WTO) in 1995. The [Asia-Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia-Pacific "Asia-Pacific") economies of the [Four Asian Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_Asian_Tigers "Four Asian Tigers"), [ASEAN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASEAN "ASEAN"), Australia and Japan were hampered by the [1997 Asian financial crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_Asian_financial_crisis "1997 Asian financial crisis") and [early 1990s recession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_1990s_recession "Early 1990s recession").

Major wars that began include the [First](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Congo_War "First Congo War") and [Second Congo Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Congo_War "Second Congo War"), the [Rwandan Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rwandan_Civil_War "Rwandan Civil War") and [genocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rwandan_genocide "Rwandan genocide"), the [Somali Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somali_Civil_War "Somali Civil War"), and [Sierra Leone Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Leone_Civil_War "Sierra Leone Civil War") in [Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa "Africa"); the [Yugoslav Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yugoslav_Wars "Yugoslav Wars") and [Bosnian Genocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnian_Genocide "Bosnian Genocide") in [Southeast Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Europe "Southeast Europe"); the [First](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Chechen_War "First Chechen War") and [Second Chechen Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Chechen_War "Second Chechen War"), in the former Soviet Union; and the [Gulf War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_War "Gulf War") in the [Middle East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_East "Middle East"). The [Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghanistan_conflict_(1978%E2%80%93present) "Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)") and [Colombian conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_conflict "Colombian conflict") continued. The [Oslo Accords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oslo_Accords "Oslo Accords") seemed to herald an end to the [Israeli–Palestinian conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli%E2%80%93Palestinian_conflict "Israeli–Palestinian conflict"), but this was in vain. However, in [Northern Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland "Northern Ireland"), [the Troubles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Troubles "The Troubles") came to a standstill in 1998 with the [Good Friday Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Friday_Agreement "Good Friday Agreement"), ending 30 years of violence.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s#cite_note-8)

### International wars

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1990s&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: International wars")]

*   The Congo Wars began in the 1990s.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s#cite_note-9)
    *   The [First Congo War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Congo_War "First Congo War") (24 October 1996 – 16 May 1997) resulted in the overthrow of dictator [Mobutu Sese Seko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobutu_Sese_Seko "Mobutu Sese Seko"), following his 32-year rule of [Zaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaire "Zaire"), which was then renamed the [Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo "Democratic Republic of the Congo").
    *   The [Second Congo War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Congo_War "Second Congo War") (August 1998 – July 2003) started in [Central Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Africa "Central Africa") and involved multiple nearby nations.

*   The [Gulf War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_War "Gulf War") (2 August 1990 – 28 February 1991). 
    *   Iraq was left in severe debt after the [Iran–Iraq War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran%E2%80%93Iraq_War "Iran–Iraq War") in the 1980s. President [Saddam Hussein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddam_Hussein "Saddam Hussein") accused [Kuwait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuwait "Kuwait") of flooding the oil market, therefore driving down prices. As a result, Iraqi forces [invaded and conquered Kuwait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Kuwait "Invasion of Kuwait").
    *   The UN ([United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations")) immediately condemned the action and a coalition force led by the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") was sent to the [Persian Gulf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_Gulf "Persian Gulf"). [Aerial bombing of Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_War_air_campaign "Gulf War air campaign") began in January 1991, and one month later, the UN forces drove the Iraqi army from Kuwait in four days.

*   Two wars were fought in the region of [Chechnya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chechnya "Chechnya"): 
    *   The [First Chechen War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Chechen_War "First Chechen War") (1994–1996) was a conflict between the [Russian Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia") and the [Chechen Republic of Ichkeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chechen_Republic_of_Ichkeria "Chechen Republic of Ichkeria"). After the initial campaign of 1994–1995, culminating in the devastating [Battle of Grozny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Grozny_(August_1996) "Battle of Grozny (August 1996)"), Russian federal forces attempted to seize control of the mountainous area of Chechnya. Despite Russia's overwhelming manpower, weaponry, and [air support](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_support "Air support"), they were set back by Chechen [guerrillas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guerrilla_warfare "Guerrilla warfare") and raids on the flatlands. The resulting widespread demoralization of Russian federal forces, and the universal[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] opposition of the Russian public to the conflict, led [Boris Yeltsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin "Boris Yeltsin")'s government to declare a [ceasefire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceasefire "Ceasefire") in 1996 and sign a [peace treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_treaty "Peace treaty") a year later.
    *   The [Second Chechen War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Chechen_War "Second Chechen War") (1999 – 2009) was started by the Russian Federation in response to the [1999 invasion of Dagestan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Dagestan_(1999) "Invasion of Dagestan (1999)") and the [Russian apartment bombings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_apartment_bombings "Russian apartment bombings"), which were blamed on the Chechens. In this military campaign, Russian forces largely recaptured the separatist region of Chechnya[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] and the outcome of the First Chechen War – in which the region gained de facto independence as the Chechen Republic of Ichkeria – was essentially reversed.

*   The [Eritrean–Ethiopian War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eritrean%E2%80%93Ethiopian_War "Eritrean–Ethiopian War") (1998–2000) was commenced by the invasion of [Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia "Ethiopia") by [Eritrea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eritrea "Eritrea") due to a territorial dispute.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s#cite_note-10) The conflict resulted in tens of thousands of deaths on both sides[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s#cite_note-Tens-of-thousands-11) and a peace agreement in December 2000.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s#cite_note-12)
*   The [Kargil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kargil_War "Kargil War") (1999) began in May when Pakistan covertly made troops to occupy strategic peaks in [Kashmir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kashmir "Kashmir"). A month later, the [Kargil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kargil_War "Kargil War") with India resulted in a political fiasco for Pakistani prime minister [Nawaz Sharif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nawaz_Sharif "Nawaz Sharif"), followed by a Pakistani military withdrawal to the [Line of Control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_of_Control "Line of Control"). The incident led to a Pakistani [military coup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_Pakistani_coup_d'%C3%A9tat "1999 Pakistani coup d'état") in October, in which Sharif was ousted by [Army Chief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_of_Army_Staff_(Pakistan) "Chief of Army Staff (Pakistan)")[Pervez Musharraf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pervez_Musharraf "Pervez Musharraf"). This conflict remains the only war fought between the two declared nuclear powers.

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/0/02/Evstafiev-sarajevo-building-burns.jpg/250px-Evstafiev-sarajevo-building-burns.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Evstafiev-sarajevo-building-burns.jpg)

[Executive council building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece%E2%80%93Bosnia_and_Herzegovina_Friendship_Building "Greece–Bosnia and Herzegovina Friendship Building") burns in [Sarajevo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarajevo "Sarajevo") after being hit by Bosnian Serb artillery in the [Bosnian War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnian_War "Bosnian War").

*   The [Yugoslav Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yugoslav_Wars "Yugoslav Wars") (1991–2001) followed the [breakup of Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakup_of_Yugoslavia "Breakup of Yugoslavia"), beginning on 25 June 1991, after the republics of [Croatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia "Croatia") and [Slovenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovenia "Slovenia") declared independence from [Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yugoslavia "Yugoslavia"). These wars were notorious for war crimes and human rights violations, including [ethnic cleansing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnic_cleansing "Ethnic cleansing") and [genocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genocide "Genocide"), with the overwhelming majority of casualties being Muslim [Bosniaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosniaks "Bosniaks"). 
    *   The [Ten-Day War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ten-Day_War "Ten-Day War") (1991) was a brief military conflict between Slovenian TO ([Slovenian Territorial Defence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovenian_Territorial_Defence "Slovenian Territorial Defence")) and the [Yugoslav People's Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yugoslav_People's_Army "Yugoslav People's Army") ("JNA") following [Slovenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovenia "Slovenia")'s declaration of independence.
    *   The [Croatian War of Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatian_War_of_Independence "Croatian War of Independence") (1991–1995) was fought in modern-day [Croatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia "Croatia") between the Croatian government (having declared independence from the [Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_Federal_Republic_of_Yugoslavia "Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia")) and both the [Yugoslav People's Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yugoslav_People's_Army "Yugoslav People's Army") ("JNA") and [Serb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbs_of_Croatia "Serbs of Croatia") forces, who established the self-proclaimed [Republic of Serbian Krajina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Serbian_Krajina "Republic of Serbian Krajina") ("RSK") within Croatia.
    *   The [Bosnian War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnian_War "Bosnian War") (1992–1995) involved several [ethnically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnicity "Ethnicity")-defined factions within [Bosnia and Herzegovina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Bosnia and Herzegovina"): [Bosniaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosniaks "Bosniaks"), [Serbs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbs "Serbs"), and [Croats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croats "Croats"), as well as [a smaller Bosniak faction led by Fikret Abdić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_Province_of_Western_Bosnia "Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia"). The [Siege of Sarajevo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Sarajevo "Siege of Sarajevo") (1992–1995) marked the most violent [urban warfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_warfare "Urban warfare") in Europe since [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") at that time, as [Serb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbs "Serbs") forces bombarded and attacked Bosnian-controlled and populated areas of the city. War crimes occurred, including [ethnic cleansing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnic_cleansing "Ethnic cleansing") and the destruction of civilian property.
    *   The final fighting in the Croatian and Bosnian wars ended in 1995 with the success of Croatian military offensives against Serb forces. This led to the mass exodus of Serbs from Croatia, Serb losses to Croat and Bosniak forces, and the signing of the [Dayton Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dayton_Agreement "Dayton Agreement"), which internally partitioned Bosnia and Herzegovina into a [Republika Srpska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republika_Srpska "Republika Srpska") and a [Bosniak-Croat Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_of_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina").

*   The [Kosovo War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kosovo_War "Kosovo War") (1998–1999) was a war between Albanian separatists and Yugoslav military and Serb paramilitary forces in [Kosovo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kosovo "Kosovo"). That conflict began in 1996 and escalated in 1998, with increasing reports of atrocities. 
    *   In 1999, the [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO "NATO"), led by the United States, launched [air attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_NATO_bombing_of_the_Federal_Republic_of_Yugoslavia "1999 NATO bombing of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia") against [Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Republic_of_Yugoslavia "Federal Republic of Yugoslavia") (then composed of only [Serbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia "Serbia") and [Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro")) to pressure the Yugoslav government to end its military operations against Albanian separatists in [Kosovo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kosovo "Kosovo"). The intervention lacked UN approval yet was justified by NATO based on accusations of war crimes committed by Yugoslav military forces working alongside nationalist Serb paramilitary groups. Finally, after months of bombing, Yugoslavia conceded to NATO's demands, and NATO forces (later UN peacekeeping forces) occupied Kosovo.

*   The [South African Border War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_African_Border_War "South African Border War") (1990) was a border war between [Zambia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zambia "Zambia"), [Angola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angola "Angola"), and [Namibia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia "Namibia") that began in 1966 and ended in 1990.

[Rwandan genocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rwandan_genocide "Rwandan genocide"): Bones of genocide victims in Murambi Technical School. Estimates put the death toll of the Rwandan genocide as high as 800,000 people.

*   The [First Liberian Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Liberian_Civil_War "First Liberian Civil War") occurred from 1989 until 1997, and led to the death of around 200,000 people.
*   The [Ethiopian Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopian_Civil_War "Ethiopian Civil War") (1991) was an internal conflict that had been raging for over twenty years. Its end coincided with the establishment of a coalition government of various factions.
*   The [Algerian Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algerian_Civil_War "Algerian Civil War") (1991–2002) was caused by a group of high-ranking army officers canceling the first multi-party elections in [Algeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algeria "Algeria").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s#cite_note-13)
*   The [Somali Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somali_Civil_War "Somali Civil War") (1991–present) included the [Battle of Mogadishu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Mogadishu_(1993) "Battle of Mogadishu (1993)").
*   The [Rwandan genocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rwandan_genocide "Rwandan genocide") (1994) occurred from 6 April to mid-July 1994 when hundreds of thousands of [Rwanda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rwanda "Rwanda")'s [Tutsis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tutsis "Tutsis") and [Hutu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hutu "Hutu") political moderates [were killed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rwandan_genocide "Rwandan genocide") by the [Hutu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hutu "Hutu")-dominated government under the [Hutu Power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hutu_Power "Hutu Power") ideology. For approximately 100 days between 500,000[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s#cite_note-A-14) and 1,000,000[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s#cite_note-15) people were killed. The United Nations and major states came under criticism for failing to stop the genocide.
*   [1993 Russian constitutional crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_Russian_constitutional_crisis "1993 Russian constitutional crisis") resulted from a severe [political deadlock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_deadlock "Political deadlock") between Russian president [Boris Yeltsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin "Boris Yeltsin") and the [Supreme Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Soviet_of_Russia "Supreme Soviet of Russia") (Russia's parliament at this time) resulting in Yeltsin ordering the controversial shelling of the Russian parliament building by tanks.
*   The [Tajikistani Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tajikistani_Civil_War "Tajikistani Civil War") (1992–1997) occurred when the [Tajikistan government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politics_of_Tajikistan "Politics of Tajikistan") was pitted against the [United Tajik Opposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Tajik_Opposition "United Tajik Opposition"), resulting in the death of between 50,000 and 100,000 people.
*   The [Zapatista uprising](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zapatista_uprising "Zapatista uprising") (1994) occurred when a large number of the Zapatista indigenous people of [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico") formed the [Zapatista Army of National Liberation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zapatista_Army_of_National_Liberation "Zapatista Army of National Liberation") and began an armed conflict with the Mexican government to protest against [NAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NAFTA "NAFTA"). The uprising lasted 12 days, bringing worldwide attention to the Zapatistas, and continued through the rest of the 1990s.
*   The [Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_Emirate_of_Afghanistan_(1996%E2%80%932001) "Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan (1996–2001)") (1996–2001) was formed at the end of the [Afghan Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_Civil_War_(1992%E2%80%931996) "Afghan Civil War (1992–1996)"), when the [Taliban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taliban "Taliban") seized control of [Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghanistan "Afghanistan") in 1996. They ruled during the [later Afghan Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_Civil_War_(1996%E2%80%932001) "Afghan Civil War (1996–2001)") until their ousting 2001.
*   [The Troubles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Troubles "The Troubles") in [Northern Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland "Northern Ireland") (1998) involved 30 years of conflict that ended on 10 April 1998, when the [Good Friday Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Friday_Agreement "Good Friday Agreement") was signed.
*   [1999 East Timorese crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_East_Timorese_crisis "1999 East Timorese crisis").

*   [Markale market massacres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markale_massacres "Markale massacres") in [Bosnia and Herzegovina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Bosnia and Herzegovina") (1994) – soldiers of the [Army of Republika Srpska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_of_Republika_Srpska "Army of Republika Srpska") deliberately targeted [Bosniak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosniaks "Bosniaks") (then known as "Bosnian Muslims") civilians.
*   [AMIA bombing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMIA_bombing "AMIA bombing") (1994) – on 18 July 1994, an unknown terrorist targeting [Argentina's Jewish community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentinian_Jew "Argentinian Jew") planted a [car bomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Car_bomb "Car bomb") in the [Asociación Mutual Israelita Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asociaci%C3%B3n_Mutual_Israelita_Argentina "Asociación Mutual Israelita Argentina") headquarters in [Buenos Aires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buenos_Aires "Buenos Aires"), killing 85 people and injuring hundreds, making it the first ethnically targeted bombing and deadliest bombing in Argentine history.

The deep-rooted animosity was heavily exacerbated by remnants of colonial racial classification. It was one of the worst genocides in history.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s#cite_note-16)
*   [Srebrenica genocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Srebrenica_genocide "Srebrenica genocide") in Bosnia and Herzegovina (1995) – soldiers of the [Army of Republika Srpska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_of_Republika_Srpska "Army of Republika Srpska") and members of [Serbia's Scorpions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scorpions_(paramilitary) "Scorpions (paramilitary)") paramilitary group committed mass murder of Bosniak civilians.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
*   [Oklahoma City bombing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_City_bombing "Oklahoma City bombing") (1995) in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") – the bombing of a federal building in [Oklahoma City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_City "Oklahoma City"), [Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma "Oklahoma") killed 168 people, becoming the deadliest terrorist attack in the United States at that time. Suspect [Timothy McVeigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothy_McVeigh "Timothy McVeigh") claimed he bombed the building in retaliation for the 1992 [Ruby Ridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruby_Ridge "Ruby Ridge") standoff and the [Waco siege](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waco_siege "Waco siege") a year later.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s#cite_note-17)
*   The [1996 Manchester bombing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Manchester_bombing "1996 Manchester bombing") (1996) – on 15 June 1996, the IRA set off a bomb in [Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester "Manchester"), England. The bomb, placed in a van on Corporation Street in the city center, targeted the city's infrastructure and economy and caused widespread damage, estimated by insurers at £700 million (£1 billion as of 2011[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1990s&action=edit)). Two hundred and twelve people were injured, but there were no fatalities.
*   The [1998 United States embassy bombings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_United_States_embassy_bombings "1998 United States embassy bombings") – [Al-Qaeda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qaeda "Al-Qaeda") militants carried out bomb attacks on United States embassies in [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") and [Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania "Tanzania"). In retaliation, U.S. naval military forces launched [cruise missile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cruise_missile "Cruise missile") attacks against Al-Qaeda bases in [Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghanistan "Afghanistan").
*   The [Omagh bombing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omagh_bombing "Omagh bombing") in [Northern Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland "Northern Ireland") (1998) – a bombing in [Omagh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omagh "Omagh"), [County Tyrone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Tyrone "County Tyrone"), that killed 29 civilians and injured hundreds more.
*   [LAX bombing plot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_millennium_attack_plots#LAX_bombing_plot "2000 millennium attack plots") (1999) – [Ahmed Ressam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Ressam "Ahmed Ressam"), an [Islamist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamism "Islamism") militant associated with Al-Qaeda, was arrested when attempting to cross from Canada into the United States at the Canada-U.S. border on 14 December 1999. It was later discovered that he intended to bomb [Los Angeles International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_International_Airport "Los Angeles International Airport") (LAX) during [millennium celebrations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennium_celebrations "Millennium celebrations"). This was the first major attempted terrorist attack by Al-Qaeda on United States soil since the [1993 World Trade Center bombing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_World_Trade_Center_bombing "1993 World Trade Center bombing") and marked the beginning of a series of attempted terrorist attacks by Al-Qaeda against the United States that would continue into the 21st century.

### Decolonization and independence

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1990s&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Decolonization and independence")]

*   [Independence of Namibia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independence_of_Namibia "Independence of Namibia") (1990) – the [Republic of Namibia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia "Namibia") gained independence from [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa") on 21 March 1990. [Walvis Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walvis_Bay "Walvis Bay"), initially retained by South Africa, joined Namibia in 1994.
*   [Breakup of Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakup_of_Yugoslavia "Breakup of Yugoslavia") (1991–1992) – the republics of [Croatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia "Croatia"), [Slovenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovenia "Slovenia"), [Bosnia and Herzegovina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Bosnia and Herzegovina"), and [Macedonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macedonia_(country) "Macedonia (country)") declared independence from [Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_Federal_Republic_of_Yugoslavia "Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia").
*   [Independence of Eritrea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independence_of_Eritrea "Independence of Eritrea") (1993) – [Eritrea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eritrea "Eritrea") gained independence from [Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia "Ethiopia").
*   [Dissolution of Czechoslovakia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dissolution_of_Czechoslovakia "Dissolution of Czechoslovakia") (1993) – the [Slovak Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovak_Republic "Slovak Republic") adopts the [Declaration of Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovak_National_Council's_Declaration_of_Independence_of_the_Slovak_Nation "Slovak National Council's Declaration of Independence of the Slovak Nation") from the [Czech and Slovak Federative Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_and_Slovak_Federative_Republic "Czech and Slovak Federative Republic") ([Czechoslovakia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czechoslovakia "Czechoslovakia")).
*   [Independence of Palau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Palau#Post-war_development "History of Palau") (1994) – [Palau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palau "Palau") gained independence from the [United Nations Trusteeship Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Trusteeship_Council "United Nations Trusteeship Council").
*   [Handover of Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handover_of_Hong_Kong "Handover of Hong Kong") (1997) – The [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") handed sovereignty of [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong") (then [British Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Hong_Kong "British Hong Kong")) to the [People's Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Republic_of_China "People's Republic of China") on 1 July 1997.
*   [Independence of East Timorese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_East_Timorese_independence_referendum "1999 East Timorese independence referendum") (1999) – [East Timor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Timor "East Timor") broke away from [Indonesian occupation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesian_occupation_of_East_Timor "Indonesian occupation of East Timor"), only a year after the fall of [Suharto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suharto "Suharto") from power, ending a 24-year [guerrilla war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guerrilla_warfare "Guerrilla warfare") and [genocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genocide "Genocide") with more than 200,000 casualties. The UN deployed a peacekeeping force spearheaded by Australia's armed forces. The United States deployed police officers to serve with the [Interpol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpol "Interpol") element to help train and equip an East Timorese police force.
*   [Handover of Macau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handover_of_Macau "Handover of Macau") (1999) – [Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Empire "Portuguese Empire") handed sovereignty of [Macau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macau "Macau") ([Portuguese Macau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Macau "Portuguese Macau")) to the People's Republic of China on 20 December 1999.
*   [Dissolution of the Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Soviet_Union "Dissolution of the Soviet Union") (1991) – multiple [Soviet Socialist Republics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republics_of_the_Soviet_Union "Republics of the Soviet Union") (SSRs) declared independence from the [USSR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_of_Soviet_Socialist_Republics "Union of Soviet Socialist Republics"). 
    *   [Armenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenia "Armenia") – the [Armenian SSR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenian_Soviet_Socialist_Republic "Armenian Soviet Socialist Republic") became the Republic of Armenia following the [Declaration of Independence of Armenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_of_State_Sovereignty_of_Armenia "Declaration of State Sovereignty of Armenia").
    *   [Azerbaijan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azerbaijan "Azerbaijan") – the [Azerbaijan SSR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azerbaijan_Soviet_Socialist_Republic "Azerbaijan Soviet Socialist Republic") became the Republic of Azerbaijan.
    *   [Belarus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belarus "Belarus") – the [Byelorussian SSR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byelorussian_Soviet_Socialist_Republic "Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic") became the Republic of Belarus following its [Declaration of State Sovereignty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_of_State_Sovereignty_of_the_Belarusian_Soviet_Socialist_Republic "Declaration of State Sovereignty of the Belarusian Soviet Socialist Republic").

### Political trends

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1990s&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Political trends")]

*   The 1990s saw an increased spread of [capitalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitalism "Capitalism") and [third way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Way "Third Way") policies.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s#cite_note-between-18) The former countries of the [Warsaw Pact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warsaw_Pact "Warsaw Pact") moved from single-party socialist states to multi-party states with private sector economies.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s#cite_note-between-18) The same wave of political liberalization occurred in the capitalist and [newly industrialized countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newly_industrialized_country "Newly industrialized country") (including [First](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_World "First World") and [Third World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_World "Third World") countries), such as [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina "Argentina"), [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil"), [Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chile "Chile"), [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India"), [Indonesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesia "Indonesia"), [Malaysia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysia "Malaysia"), [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico"), the [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines"), [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa"), [South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea "South Korea"), [Taiwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiwan "Taiwan"), and [Thailand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thailand "Thailand"). Market reforms made incredible changes to the economies of [Second World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World "Second World") socialist countries such as [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") and [Vietnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam "Vietnam").
*   Ethnic tensions and violence in [former Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_Federal_Republic_of_Yugoslavia "Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia") during the 1990s created a greater sense of ethnic identity among nations in newly independent countries and a marked increase in the popularity of nationalism.

#### Africa

[Nelson Mandela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Mandela "Nelson Mandela") voting in 1994, after thirty years of imprisonment.

*   [African National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_National_Congress "African National Congress") leader [Nelson Mandela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Mandela "Nelson Mandela") was released from prison on 11 February 1990, after thirty years of imprisonment for opposing [apartheid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa_under_apartheid "South Africa under apartheid") and white-minority rule in South Africa. [Apartheid ended](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Negotiations_to_end_apartheid_in_South_Africa "Negotiations to end apartheid in South Africa") in South Africa in 1994.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s#cite_note-mandela-19)

#### Americas

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1990s&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Americas")]

[Video 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/06/Response_to_the_Lewinsky_Allegations_%28January_26%2C_1998%29_Bill_Clinton.ogv?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=rest&utm_content=original)

During the late 1990s, a move was made to remove American president [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") from power following the [Clinton–Lewinsky scandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton%E2%80%93Lewinsky_scandal "Clinton–Lewinsky scandal"). This [impeachment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment_of_Bill_Clinton "Impeachment of Bill Clinton") attempt did not succeed, and Clinton continued to serve as president until the end of his term in January 2001.

*   The [Argentine peso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentine_peso "Argentine peso") was pegged to the [American dollar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar") by the [Convertibility plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convertibility_plan "Convertibility plan") by the government of [Carlos Menem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Menem "Carlos Menem") in an attempt to eliminate [hyperinflation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperinflation "Hyperinflation") and stimulate [economic growth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_growth "Economic growth"). While it was initially met with considerable success, the board's actions ultimately failed. The Convertibility Plan went from 1991 to 2002.
*   The establishment of the [North American Free Trade Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_Free_Trade_Agreement "North American Free Trade Agreement") (NAFTA) on 1 January 1994, created a North American [free-trade zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free-trade_zone "Free-trade zone") consisting of Canada, Mexico, and the United States.
*   The [Constitution of Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Argentina "Constitution of Argentina") went through an important [reform in 1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_amendment_of_the_Constitution_of_Argentina "1994 amendment of the Constitution of Argentina"), which introduced [third generation rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_generations_of_human_rights "Three generations of human rights"), gave more relevance to [international treaties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty "Treaty"), and also introduced new concepts such as [Necessity and Urgency Decrees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Necessity_and_Urgency_Decree "Necessity and Urgency Decree") and the [two-round system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-round_system "Two-round system").
*   Canadian politics was radically altered in the [1993 federal election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_Canadian_federal_election "1993 Canadian federal election") with the collapse of the [Progressive Conservative Party of Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_Conservative_Party_of_Canada "Progressive Conservative Party of Canada"). A major political party in Canada since 1867, the party went from controlling the government to being left with only two seats. The [New Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Democratic_Party_(Canada) "New Democratic Party (Canada)") collapsed as well, with their sets declining from 44 to 9. The [Liberal Party of Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Party_of_Canada "Liberal Party of Canada") was the only genuinely 'national' political party left standing. Regionally based parties, such as the Quebec-based [Bloc Québécois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloc_Qu%C3%A9b%C3%A9cois "Bloc Québécois") and the almost entirely Western Canada-based [Reform Party of Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reform_Party_of_Canada "Reform Party of Canada"), rose from political insignificance to being major political parties.
*   After the collapse of the [Meech Lake constitutional accord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meech_Lake_Accord "Meech Lake Accord") in 1990, the province of [Quebec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec "Quebec") in Canada experienced a rekindled wave of separatism by [Francophone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francophone "Francophone")[Québécois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qu%C3%A9b%C3%A9cois_people "Québécois people") nationalists, who sought for Quebec to become an independent country and forced a referendum on the question of independence in 1995. 
    *   The [1995 Quebec referendum on sovereignty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_Quebec_independence_referendum "1995 Quebec independence referendum") was held in the predominantly francophone province of Quebec in Canada, a majority [Anglophone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglophone "Anglophone") country. If accepted, Quebec would have become an independent country with an economic association with Canada. Quebec's voters narrowly rejected the proposal.

*   [Jean-Bertrand Aristide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Bertrand_Aristide "Jean-Bertrand Aristide"), a former Haitian priest, became the first democratically elected President of [Haiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haiti "Haiti") in 1990. A proponent of liberation theology, Aristide was appointed to a Roman Catholic parish in [Port-au-Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port-au-Prince "Port-au-Prince") in 1982 after completing his studies to become a priest of the Salesian order. Aristide was later forced into exile in the Central African Republic and South Africa and returned to Haiti after several years.
*   [Ernesto Zedillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernesto_Zedillo "Ernesto Zedillo") was elected [President of Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Mexico "President of Mexico") in the [1994 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Mexican_general_election "1994 Mexican general election"), making him the last of an uninterrupted 72-year-long succession of Mexican presidents from the dominant [Institutional Revolutionary Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institutional_Revolutionary_Party "Institutional Revolutionary Party") (PRI). The original PRI candidate, [Luis Donaldo Colosio Murrieta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Donaldo_Colosio_Murrieta "Luis Donaldo Colosio Murrieta"), was assassinated several months prior.
*   Due to [internal conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_conflict_in_Peru "Internal conflict in Peru") and an economic crisis, [Alberto Fujimori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_Fujimori "Alberto Fujimori") rose to power in [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru "Peru") and remained in office for eleven years. His administration was marked by economic development but also by numerous human rights violations ([La Cantuta massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Cantuta_massacre "La Cantuta massacre"), [Barrios Altos massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barrios_Altos_massacre "Barrios Altos massacre")) and a rampant corruption network set up by [Vladimiro Montesinos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimiro_Montesinos "Vladimiro Montesinos").
*   The sluggish [Latin American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_America "Latin America") economies of [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina "Argentina"), [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil"), [Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chile "Chile"), and [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico"), by a new emphasis on [free markets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_market "Free market") for all their citizens after the [debt crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_American_debt_crisis "Latin American debt crisis") of the 1980s. Following democratic reforms and neoliberal policies were implemented by President [Carlos Saúl Menem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Sa%C3%BAl_Menem "Carlos Saúl Menem") (Argentina), President [Eduardo Frei Ruiz-Tagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eduardo_Frei_Ruiz-Tagle "Eduardo Frei Ruiz-Tagle") (Chile), President [Ernesto Zedillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernesto_Zedillo "Ernesto Zedillo") (Mexico), and President [Fernando Henrique Cardoso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Henrique_Cardoso "Fernando Henrique Cardoso") (Brazil), in their best shape by the late 1990s.
*   [United States President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") Bill Clinton was a dominant political figure in international affairs during the 1990s, known primarily for his attempts to negotiate peace in the Middle East and end the ongoing wars occurring in the former Yugoslavia, his promotion of international action to decrease human-created [climate change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change "Climate change"), and his endorsement of advancing [free trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_trade "Free trade") in the Americas.
*   [After a failed coup attempt in 1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_1992_Venezuelan_coup_d'%C3%A9tat_attempt "February 1992 Venezuelan coup d'état attempt"), [Hugo Chávez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugo_Ch%C3%A1vez "Hugo Chávez"), politician and former member of the Venezuelan military, is [elected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_Venezuelan_presidential_election "1998 Venezuelan presidential election") President of [Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuela "Venezuela") in 1998.
*   [Lewinsky scandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewinsky_scandal "Lewinsky scandal") – US president Bill Clinton was caught in a media-frenzied scandal involving inappropriate relations with White House intern [Monica Lewinsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monica_Lewinsky "Monica Lewinsky"), which was first announced on 21 January 1998. After the United States House of Representatives [impeached Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment_of_Bill_Clinton "Impeachment of Bill Clinton") on 19 December 1998, for perjury under oath, and following an investigation by federal prosecutor [Kenneth Starr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Starr "Kenneth Starr"), the Senate acquitted Clinton of all charges on 12 February 1999. He served out the remainder of his second term.
*   California voters passed [Proposition 215](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Proposition_215_(1996) "California Proposition 215 (1996)") in 1996, which legalized [cannabis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannabis_(drug) "Cannabis (drug)") for medicinal purposes.

#### Asia

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/Bill_Clinton%2C_Yitzhak_Rabin%2C_Yasser_Arafat_at_the_White_House_1993-09-13.jpg/250px-Bill_Clinton%2C_Yitzhak_Rabin%2C_Yasser_Arafat_at_the_White_House_1993-09-13.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bill_Clinton,_Yitzhak_Rabin,_Yasser_Arafat_at_the_White_House_1993-09-13.jpg)

[Israeli Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Israel "Prime Minister of Israel")[Yitzhak Rabin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yitzhak_Rabin "Yitzhak Rabin"), [United States President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States")[Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton"), and [Palestine Liberation Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestine_Liberation_Organization "Palestine Liberation Organization") (PLO) Chairman [Yasser Arafat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasser_Arafat "Yasser Arafat") during the signing of the [Oslo Accords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oslo_Accords "Oslo Accords") on 13 September 1993.

*   In 1990, the [Lebanese Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanese_Civil_War "Lebanese Civil War") came to a close and a return to political normalcy in [Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon "Lebanon") began. With peace among all factions in Lebanon, the rebuilding of the country and its capital, [Beirut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beirut "Beirut"), began.
*   [1990 Nepalese revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_Nepalese_revolution "1990 Nepalese revolution"), a multiparty movement against the one-party Panchayat rule in Nepal. It led to the end of absolute monarchy in Nepal and the restoration of democracy.
*   [Israeli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel") Prime Minister [Yitzhak Rabin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yitzhak_Rabin "Yitzhak Rabin") and [Palestinian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_people "Palestinian people") Prime Minister [Yasser Arafat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasser_Arafat "Yasser Arafat") agree to the [Israeli–Palestinian peace process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli%E2%80%93Palestinian_peace_process "Israeli–Palestinian peace process") at the culmination of the [Oslo Accords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oslo_Accords "Oslo Accords"), negotiated by the United States president, Bill Clinton, on 13 September 1993. 
    *   By signing the Oslo accords, the [Palestine Liberation Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestine_Liberation_Organization "Palestine Liberation Organization") recognized Israel's right to exist. At the same time, Israel permitted the creation of an autonomous [Palestinian National Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_National_Authority "Palestinian National Authority") consisting of the [Gaza Strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip "Gaza Strip") and [West Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bank "West Bank"), which was implemented in 1994.
